**Room Link:** https://tryhackme.com/room/boogeyman3

**Date:** 30-04-2026

# Scenario

Without tripping any security defences of Quick Logistics LLC, the Boogeyman was able to compromise one of the employees and stayed in the dark, waiting for the right moment to continue the attack. Using this initial email access, the threat actors attempted to expand the impact by targeting the CEO, Evan Hutchinson.

<img src="../../../_resources/4bc14f4d49a34c6c5e030112682ab470.png" alt="4bc14f4d49a34c6c5e030112682ab470.png" width="1175" height="488" class="jop-noMdConv">

The email appeared questionable, but Evan still opened the attachment despite the scepticism. After opening the attached document and seeing that nothing happened, Evan reported the phishing email to the security team.

## Initial Investigation

Upon receiving the phishing email report, the security team investigated the workstation of the CEO. During this activity, the team discovered the email attachment in the downloads folder of the victim.

<img src="../../../_resources/ae0a91ca7ec0d231e58b763fd99a97ef.png" alt="ae0a91ca7ec0d231e58b763fd99a97ef.png" width="1184" height="228" class="jop-noMdConv">

In addition, the security team also observed a file inside the ISO payload, as shown in the image below.

<img src="../../../_resources/edbe46a666c35d42e54d920a7fdd16d1.png" alt="edbe46a666c35d42e54d920a7fdd16d1.png" width="1061" height="400" class="jop-noMdConv">

Lastly, it was presumed by the security team that the incident occurred between **August 29 and August 30, 2023**.

# Practice

<img src="../../../_resources/89095672e9f2f08679ec9bc0d19b9cf7.png" alt="89095672e9f2f08679ec9bc0d19b9cf7.png" width="1273" height="671" class="jop-noMdConv">

At the beginning, I write a query following the name of suspicious email name. The picture above give the information that this is a file with double extension, prove that the attacker tried to trick the victim to execute this file.

- **.hta** extention is a html application file so that **mshta.exe** (system process) will responsible for running this file.

immidiately after execution, a script was runned. Seemingly, It stealthily tried to collect data on victim host or move some malicious files to another spot to evade detection.

<img src="../../../_resources/3a39cafee8e7bff69d6525d38e32dfaa.png" alt="3a39cafee8e7bff69d6525d38e32dfaa.png" width="1277" height="673" class="jop-noMdConv">

keep going with the file named review.dat, I see a command that **rundll32.exe** (system process is responsible for running (.dll, .dat) file) is implementing the **DllRegisterServer** Library in **review.dat** file.

<img src="../../../_resources/0ec38a6389dab2e52c42d3a935803e16.png" alt="0ec38a6389dab2e52c42d3a935803e16.png" width="1216" height="619" class="jop-noMdConv">

Right after that, a powershell script was activated to create a schedule Task with the name is **Review.**

<img src="../../../_resources/9a22066fa86ad0b1a6ebe4f09511fc54.png" alt="9a22066fa86ad0b1a6ebe4f09511fc54.png" width="1195" height="586" class="jop-noMdConv">

Keep follwing the file review.dat, I see alot of command that attacker use to bypass privilege (UAC bypass).

- because **fodhelper.exe** is a system service that always be runned with highest privilege.
- This specific privilege level makes **fodhelper.exe** a common target for **UAC (User Account Control) bypass** techniques.
    - Attackers exploit this by modifying registry keys at **HKCU:\\Software\\Classes\\ms-settings\\shell\\open\\command** to redirect the process to execute arbitrary commands or scripts with elevated system privileges.
    - When fodhelper.exe is activated, It will read the occupied registry key value and running the malware script.
    - Security tools and EDR solutions actively monitor for fodhelper.exe spawning unexpected child processes or accessing these specific registry paths to detect potential privilege escalation attempts.

I wanna check if any C2 connection was created, I found **wsmprovhost.exe** service running (system service responsible for windows remote management, Powershell remoting, etc.)

<img src="../../../_resources/9e04a4f75fb42d598fa4c2f88624ab9e.png" alt="9e04a4f75fb42d598fa4c2f88624ab9e.png" width="1135" height="636" class="jop-noMdConv">

because source IP of the victim host is 10.10.155.159, I notice about the top IP traffic **165.232.170.151:80** that the victim comunicating with.

<img src="../../../_resources/1f03381b7844ac9bbb0fccbbcf101c11.png" alt="1f03381b7844ac9bbb0fccbbcf101c11.png" width="1357" height="737" class="jop-noMdConv">

by looking up on **virusTotal**, It was flagged as Malicious.

<img src="../../../_resources/a15b4d15e54bdb496ea5a611d9d75a4d.png" alt="a15b4d15e54bdb496ea5a611d9d75a4d.png" width="1346" height="644" class="jop-noMdConv">

I detect that the attacker downloaded **Mimikatz** tool from internet and save in into **C:\\Windows\\Temp\\x64\\** Directory named **mimi.zip.** Lets see what was going on previously.

<img src="../../../_resources/a56bcf06db0a1dfcdb378659d041cde7.png" alt="a56bcf06db0a1dfcdb378659d041cde7.png" width="1327" height="635" class="jop-noMdConv">

It is the command runned by malicious file **review.dat** earlier.

<img src="../../../_resources/fbcdd4ea545420dbad205e098be463f8.png" alt="fbcdd4ea545420dbad205e098be463f8.png" width="1535" height="294" class="jop-noMdConv">

This is what we have when decode the base64 string.

![a49bf8736bddeca6ed638ccd736d0934.png](../../../_resources/a49bf8736bddeca6ed638ccd736d0934.png)

I keep decoding base64 string then take the C2 server domain name **http://cdn.bananapeelparty.net:80**
